instruction: Extract a still frame from this video at the 10-second mark and save it as 'frame_10s.png' on the Desktop.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully flipped an upside-down video using ffmpeg vflip filter and saved it with a new name. First tried VLC UI Effects dialog but couldn't find flip option, then switched to terminal and ffmpeg.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate VLC menus, open terminal with Ctrl+Alt+T, use ffmpeg for video transformations, handle ffmpeg prompts, verify file creation
metadata.task_rationale: Tests a different ffmpeg capability (frame extraction) using the same video. Agent demonstrated ffmpeg proficiency and should be able to use ffmpeg -ss to extract a frame as PNG.
metadata.explanation: Task requires extracting a single frame at the 10-second mark from the video and saving as PNG. Evaluator checks the output file exists at /home/user/Desktop/frame_10s.png and has a reasonable file size (>500 bytes).

scoring_breakdown.file_exists: 0.7 - PNG image file exists at expected path
scoring_breakdown.valid_size: 0.3 - File has reasonable size (>500 bytes, indicating a valid image)

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly checks file existence and size at /home/user/Desktop/frame_10s.png using bash stat command, with proper error handling for missing files and parse failures.
Metric correctly handles expected parameter for type='rule': expected IS the rules dict {'min_file_size': 500}, and expected.get('min_file_size', 100) accesses it correctly.
Scoring breakdown (0.7 file exists + 0.3 size check) is reasonable for this task.

Coverage gap: Evaluator does NOT verify the frame is from the 10-second mark of the video. Any PNG file at the correct path with size >500 bytes would pass, even if extracted from a different timestamp or not from the video at all.
Coverage gap: Evaluator does NOT verify the file is a valid PNG image (e.g., via magic bytes or image library). A non-image file >500 bytes at the right path would score 1.0.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Add a check using 'file' command or Python PIL to verify the output is a valid PNG image, not just any file with .png extension.
Consider extracting a reference frame at the 10-second mark during setup (using ffmpeg -ss 10 -vframes 1) and comparing image similarity (e.g., SSIM or perceptual hash) to verify temporal accuracy.
At minimum, add a check that the file has PNG magic bytes (\x89PNG) to confirm it is actually an image file.
